anomalies.title: Baarle-Hertog / Baarle-Nassau
anomalies.fact: Baarle-Hertog consists of 22 Belgian enclaves inside the Netherlands; Baarle-Nassau has 7 Dutch counter-enclaves inside them plus 1 enclave in Belgium, giving the Belgium–Netherlands boundary about 31 separate segments.
anomalies.src: Wikipedia "Baarle-Hertog"; Wikipedia "List of countries and territories by number of land borders"

anomalies.title: Vennbahn enclaves
anomalies.fact: The trackbed of the former Vennbahn railway is Belgian territory, cutting off five small German enclaves between Roetgen and Monschau, so Belgium and Germany share six separate boundary segments.

anomalies.title: Madha and Nahwa
anomalies.fact: Madha is an Omani exclave (~75 km²) surrounded by the UAE, and inside it lies Nahwa, a UAE counter-enclave, so it is an enclave within an enclave.

anomalies.title: Büsingen am Hochrhein
anomalies.fact: A German municipality of about 7.6 km² entirely surrounded by Switzerland. It is part of the Swiss customs area and uses the Swiss franc in practice.

anomalies.title: Campione d'Italia
anomalies.fact: An Italian exclave of ~2.7 km² on Lake Lugano, entirely surrounded by the Swiss canton of Ticino.

anomalies.title: Llívia
anomalies.fact: A Spanish town of ~12.8 km² entirely surrounded by France. It stayed Spanish after the 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees because it was a "town" and not one of the ceded "villages".

anomalies.title: Kaliningrad Oblast
anomalies.fact: Russia's semi-exclave on the Baltic, cut off from the rest of Russia by Lithuania and Poland. Russia's whole border with each of them runs along Kaliningrad (Factbook: Lithuania 261 km, Poland 209 km).

anomalies.title: Nakhchivan
anomalies.fact: Azerbaijan's autonomous republic, separated from the rest of Azerbaijan by Armenia. It also gives Azerbaijan its only border with Turkey (Factbook 17 km; Wikipedia 9 km).
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Azerbaijan); Wikipedia "Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic"

anomalies.title: Cabinda
anomalies.fact: Angola's Cabinda Province is separated from the rest of Angola by a strip of DRC territory reaching the Atlantic. Angola's entire 231 km border with the Republic of the Congo, and 225 km of its border with the DRC, belong to Cabinda.

anomalies.title: Musandam
anomalies.fact: The Musandam Peninsula on the Strait of Hormuz is an Omani exclave, separated from the rest of Oman by the UAE.

anomalies.title: Alaska
anomalies.fact: The largest US state by area is not contiguous with the rest of the country. Its only land neighbour is Canada, along 2,475 km of the 8,891 km Canada–US boundary.

anomalies.title: Point Roberts
anomalies.fact: The tip of the Tsawwassen peninsula south of the 49th parallel is part of Washington State, but it can only be reached by land through British Columbia.

anomalies.title: Northwest Angle
anomalies.fact: The only part of the contiguous US north of the 49th parallel (Minnesota). It is reachable by land only through Manitoba, a result of a mapping error in the 1783 Treaty of Paris.

anomalies.title: Ceuta and Melilla
anomalies.fact: Two Spanish autonomous cities on the African mainland (Factbook land boundaries: Ceuta 8 km, Melilla 10.5 km). They are the EU's only land borders in Africa, and Morocco claims both.

anomalies.title: Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera
anomalies.fact: This Spanish rock was joined to the Moroccan coast by a sand isthmus in 1930 (some sources say 1934). The result is the world's shortest single land-border segment: 75 m per the Factbook, 85 m per Wikipedia's article, with 80–81 m in other sources.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Spain, note); Wikipedia "Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera"

anomalies.title: Botswana–Zambia at Kazungula
anomalies.fact: The shortest complete border between two countries is about 150 m across the Zambezi (Factbook 0.15 km). Since 2021 it has been crossed by the Kazungula Bridge.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Botswana, Zambia); Wikipedia "Kazungula Bridge"

anomalies.title: Kazungula near-quadripoint
anomalies.fact: Botswana, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe come within roughly 150 m of one another. The point was long described as the world's only quadripoint, but it actually consists of two tripoints joined by the short Botswana–Zambia boundary.

anomalies.title: Spain–Portugal, one of the oldest borders
anomalies.fact: The Spain–Portugal boundary (Factbook 1,224 km) dates largely from the 1297 Treaty of Alcañices and is often called the oldest unchanged border in Europe. Olivenza/Olivença is still disputed.

anomalies.title: Canada–United States
anomalies.fact: The longest international land border: 8,891 km per the Factbook, of which 2,475 km is with Alaska. The longest single continuous segment is Kazakhstan–Russia (7,644 km per the Factbook).

anomalies.title: Lesotho
anomalies.fact: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa (1,106 km). It is the largest of the world's three enclaved sovereign states and the only one outside Italy.

anomalies.title: Vatican City
anomalies.fact: The smallest sovereign state, entirely surrounded by Rome, Italy, with a 3.4 km boundary (Factbook; Wikipedia gives 3.2 km).

anomalies.title: San Marino
anomalies.fact: San Marino is entirely surrounded by Italy (37 km). Together with Vatican City and Lesotho it is one of only three enclaved sovereign states.

anomalies.title: Pheasant Island
anomalies.fact: An uninhabited island in the Bidasoa river, a Franco-Spanish condominium since the 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees. Administration alternates between the two countries every six months.

anomalies.title: Saint Martin
anomalies.fact: France (Saint-Martin) and the Netherlands (Sint Maarten) have shared this Caribbean island since the 1648 Treaty of Concordia. The boundary is 16 km per the Factbook and 10.2 km per Wikipedia.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Saint Martin, Sint Maarten)

anomalies.title: Hispaniola
anomalies.fact: Haiti and the Dominican Republic share Hispaniola (376 km boundary). They form their own two-node component of the contiguous land graph.

anomalies.title: Timor
anomalies.fact: Timor-Leste and Indonesia (West Timor) share the island of Timor (253 km). Timor-Leste's Oecusse district is an exclave surrounded by Indonesia on land.

anomalies.title: New Guinea
anomalies.fact: Papua New Guinea and Indonesia split New Guinea along a mostly straight 141°E meridian line with a Fly River bulge (824 km).

anomalies.title: Borneo
anomalies.fact: Borneo is the only island divided among three sovereign states. Brunei (266 km with Malaysia) is itself split in two by the Malaysian Limbang district.

anomalies.title: Ireland
anomalies.fact: Ireland and the UK share the island of Ireland (499 km). Since Brexit this has been the only land border between the UK and the EU.

anomalies.title: Bir Tawil, terra nullius
anomalies.fact: Because the 1899 and 1902 Egypt–Sudan lines differ, both countries claim the Halaib Triangle, and neither claims the ~2,060 km² Bir Tawil. It is among the few unclaimed lands on Earth.

anomalies.title: Hans Island (Tartupaluk)
anomalies.fact: Canada and Denmark/Greenland settled the 'Whisky War' with an agreement signed on 14 June 2022 that splits the 1.3 km² island and creates a ~1.3 km land boundary. Greenland's Factbook entry still lists 0 km.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Canada, Denmark); news reports 14–15 Jun 2022 (NBC/AP)

anomalies.title: Doubly landlocked: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan
anomalies.fact: These are the only two countries surrounded entirely by landlocked countries, so reaching the sea means crossing at least two borders.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (World, Land boundaries note 1)

anomalies.title: Dahala Khagrabari (historic)
anomalies.fact: Historic: this was the world's only third-order enclave, an Indian enclave inside a Bangladeshi enclave inside an Indian enclave inside Bangladesh. It was transferred to Bangladesh on 31 Jul / 1 Aug 2015 under the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement, which exchanged all 162 Cooch Behar enclaves.

anomalies.title: Gibraltar
anomalies.fact: A British Overseas Territory with a 1.2 km land border with Spain across the isthmus. Spain claims sovereignty, and a UK–EU treaty on Gibraltar's border was negotiated in 2025.

anomalies.title: Akrotiri and Dhekelia
anomalies.fact: The UK Sovereign Base Areas on Cyprus have land borders of 48 km (Akrotiri) and 108 km (Dhekelia). Dhekelia surrounds the Cypriot villages of Ormideia and Xylotymbou and also touches the UN buffer zone.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Akrotiri, Dhekelia); Wikipedia "Akrotiri and Dhekelia"

anomalies.title: France's longest border is with Brazil
anomalies.fact: Through French Guiana, France's border with Brazil (Factbook 649 km; Wikipedia 673 km) is longer than its border with Spain (646 km / 623 km). France therefore borders 11 entities here, more than any European country except Russia.

anomalies.title: China and Russia: 14 neighbours each
anomalies.fact: The Factbook notes that China and Russia each border 14 countries. In this graph China has 15 because Hong Kong is a separate entity (16 if Macau were counted). Russia would have 16 if Abkhazia and South Ossetia were counted.
anomalies.src: CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (World, note 3); Wikipedia "List of countries and territories by number of land borders"

anomalies.title: Kosovo–Serbia
anomalies.fact: Serbia treats the 366 km line as an administrative boundary and still claims a border with Albania through Kosovo. In this graph Serbia keeps direct edges to North Macedonia (101 km) and Montenegro (157 km) but has no edge to Albania.

anomalies.title: Western Sahara
anomalies.fact: The Factbook assigns the 1,564 km Western Sahara–Mauritania line to Morocco, while Wikipedia lists Western Sahara separately. Western Sahara's status is unresolved, so this edge is typed disputed.

anomalies.title: Guantánamo Bay
anomalies.fact: The US naval base has a 28.5 km perimeter, but the Factbook states that the leased base remains part of Cuba. It is not counted as a US–Cuba land border here, although Wikipedia lists one.

anomalies.title: The Gambia
anomalies.fact: The Gambia is surrounded by Senegal (749 km) on every side except a short Atlantic coast.

anomalies.title: Fergana Valley enclaves
anomalies.fact: Uzbekistan's Sokh and Shakhimardan and Tajikistan's Vorukh are enclaves inside Kyrgyzstan. Wikipedia counts 6 separate Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan boundary segments.
anomalies.src: Wikipedia "Sokh District"; Wikipedia "Vorukh"; Wikipedia "List of countries and territories by number of land borders"

anomalies.title: Passport Island (King Fahd Causeway)
anomalies.fact: Saudi Arabia and Bahrain meet on an artificial island in the middle of the causeway (~196 m boundary per Wikipedia). The Factbook lists Bahrain with 0 km of land border, so the edge is typed bridge-or-tunnel-only.
anomalies.src: Wikipedia "List of countries and territories by number of land borders"; CIA World Factbook (Jan 2026) (Bahrain)

anomalies.title: Triple Frontier
anomalies.fact: The Argentina–Brazil–Paraguay tripoint lies where the Iguazu River meets the Paraná, and each country marks it with an obelisk in its colours.

anomalies.title: Artsvashen and the Azerbaijani enclaves in Armenia
anomalies.fact: Armenia's Artsvashen exclave inside Azerbaijan and Azerbaijani exclaves inside Armenia (Karki, Yukhari Askipara, Barkhudarly) give the Armenia–Azerbaijan boundary 6 segments, per Wikipedia. Each side has controlled the other's enclaves since 1992.
anomalies.src: Wikipedia "Artsvashen"; Wikipedia "List of countries and territories by number of land borders"

factbook_total_mismatch_explanations.cuba: Factbook counts the 28.5 km Guantanamo Bay naval base perimeter; it is leased US-administered territory that Factbook itself says remains part of Cuba, so no Cuba–US edge.

km_crosscheck_vs_wikipedia.note: Wikipedia figures are systematically different (different, unstated measurement source); Factbook kept as primary. Palestine pairs were omitted because Wikipedia splits them into Gaza and West Bank rows, so they are not comparable. Denmark–Germany: Wikipedia's 68 km is a straight-line figure, versus 140 km in the Factbook.

united-states–mexico: Factbook 3,111 (US) vs 3,155 (Mexico) vs Wikipedia 3,141 → IBWC 3,145 km (1,954 mi)
israel–jordan: Factbook Israel 327 (incl. 20 km in Dead Sea, inconsistent with its own total) vs Jordan 307 → 307
ireland: Factbook total 490 but lists UK 499 → 499
canada–greenland: Factbook Greenland 0 km vs Canada/Denmark 1.3 km → 1.3 (2022 agreement)
france–netherlands (Saint Martin): Factbook 16 km vs Wikipedia 10.2 km → 16 (Factbook), flagged
Peñón de Vélez: Factbook & Wikipedia list 75 m, Wikipedia article and press 85 m (also 80/81 m) → 75 m used inside morocco–spain km
denmark–canada in Factbook reassigned to greenland–canada (Greenland is its own entity)
Morocco–Mauritania: Factbook attributes the Western Sahara line to Morocco; typed disputed, via Western Sahara
Algeria–Morocco excludes 41 km Algeria–Western Sahara segment (not attributed to any listed entity)
Serbia–Albania: Serbia claims a border via Kosovo; no de facto boundary → no edge
checks.components_note: With via-territory edges included, the Americas join Afro-Eurasia through French Guiana and Saint Martin, and Ireland–UK, Cyprus, Indonesia/PNG/Timor-Leste/Brunei/Malaysia all join as well, because entities are nodes and not landmasses. Malaysia connects Borneo to the mainland. The contiguous variant below uses only land and disputed edges.
